output.review_comment:
Two of the fixes look right: counting from the day after `start` through `end`, and returning the negated result when `end < start`. Both match the docstring.

The observed-holiday change is the problem. The original docstring said holidays are "used exactly as given: a holiday that falls on a Saturday or Sunday removes nothing and is not moved to a nearby weekday." The PR does the opposite: it moves Saturday holidays to Friday and Sunday holidays to Monday. It also rewrites the docstring to match the new code. That changes the spec agreed with the fulfilment team without telling anyone, and the PR description calls it a fix. A weekend holiday will now take a weekday out of the count, so fulfilment date calculations will change.

If a test really does expect observed-holiday behaviour, then the test and the documented spec disagree. That needs to go back to the teammate and the fulfilment team to decide. It shouldn't be settled by quietly editing the docstring so it agrees with the code. If no test needs it, this is an extra behaviour change nobody asked for.

Please revert the observed-holiday logic and the docstring edit, and use `off = set(holidays)` again. Keep the range fix and the `end < start` fix, then run the tests again. If a test still fails because it expects weekend holidays to move, report that conflict in the PR rather than working around it.
